beats.say: What if I told you America's most notorious gangster was finally jailed... over his taxes?
beats.label: AL CAPONE

beats.say: Chicago, the 1920s. Prohibition made Al Capone rich.
beats.label: 1920s

beats.say: Bootlegging, gambling, violence. Yet prosecutors could not make the big crimes stick.
beats.label: UNTOUCHABLE?

beats.say: Then in 1927, the Supreme Court ruled: even illegal income is taxable.
beats.head: U.S. v. SULLIVAN, 1927

beats.say: So a tax agent, Frank Wilson, went after his money.
beats.label: FRANK J. WILSON

beats.say: In 1930, he found ledgers, with payments marked A, and Al.
beats.head: THE LEDGER

beats.say: Sentenced to eleven years. He served about seven and a half.
beats.label: THE TIME

beats.say: From 1934, much of it on Alcatraz.
beats.label: ALCATRAZ

beats.say: He walked out in 1939, seriously ill.
beats.label: RELEASED

beats.say: Not for murder. Not for bootlegging. For taxes.
beats.label: FOR TAXES.
